note: The prototype's Settings hub (docs/superpowers/mockups/live): mod-shell.js `L.tile({area:"settings"...})` rows sh.names, sh.devices, sh.add, sh.pin, sh.session and mod-guardian.js `sr(...)` rows (lines 1305-1324), in their group order and `order` value. `{child}` is the child's name. Flutter's settings_hub_parity test holds the real hub to this list: same group, same relative order, same title. A prototype row with no Flutter counterpart says why in `flutter`. Update this file when the prototype's hub changes (the Flutter test then tells you what to build).

rows.title: Remove a device
rows.why: Removing a device is the Paired devices screen in Flutter (it lists and revokes); one row, not two.

rows.title: {partner} (simulated co-guardian)
rows.why: The prototype's second guardian is a simulation; the real one is a different person on a different device (online-parked).

rows.title: Guardian PIN
rows.why: Its explainer (ob.pinInfo) is the top card of the Change PIN screen, so Flutter has one PIN row.

rows.title: Delete my account
rows.why: Open owner decision (the 6 to 12 month recovery window): Flutter's Deletion row states what deletion means and deletes nothing here.

rows.title: Session
rows.why: The prototype's sign-in state row; Flutter's Sign out row covers it.
